claims.text: Dynamic strain aging governs the dynamic response of solidified equiatomic FeNiCrMn.
Dynamic strain aging in FeNiCrMn arises from transient solute-dislocation interactions.
At suitable temperatures and strain rates, Fe, Ni, Cr, and Mn atoms transiently cluster at dislocation cores.
Localized solute atmospheres at dislocation cores temporarily pin dislocations.
Intermittent dislocation pinning causes serrated yielding or Portevin-Le Chatelier behavior.
Dynamic strain aging produces an anomalous peak in yield stress at intermediate temperatures.
Dynamic strain aging produces rate-sensitive strengthening behavior in FeNiCrMn.
The target material is solidified, equiatomic, Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Cast or rapidly solidified FeNiCrMn has a homogeneous microstructure typical of those processing conditions.
The proposed initial state contains minimal pre-existing defects other than solidification-inherent dislocations.
Dynamic tensile tests should span strain rates from 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^2 s^-1.
The anticipated dynamic-strain-aging regime is approximately 200 K to 500 K.
Without dynamic strain aging, FeNiCrMn would exhibit a smooth load-displacement response without serrations.
Without dynamic strain aging, yield stress would vary monotonically with temperature.
Without dynamic strain aging, significant transient solute clustering at dislocation cores would not occur.
Observing serrated yielding, an intermediate-temperature yield-stress peak, and solute clustering at dislocation cores would support the proposed mechanism.
Failure to observe the specified mechanical signatures together with failure to detect dislocation-core solute clusters would falsify the hypothesis.
Microstructural heterogeneity could shift the temperature and strain-rate regimes in which dynamic strain aging is active.
